messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — High error-rate: routing misroutes & cache collisions detected in eu-west-1. Observed spike in 5xxs and wrong-model-variant responses. Automatic escalation to #incidents.

jordan-sre: I'm on call, taking pager. seeing ~15% error rate for requests routed to variant v2 instead of pinned v1. Starting investigation.

maria-ml: pinged. quick hypothesis: cache key composition may be omitting variant suffix so cached KV entries are being reused across variants when fallthrough routing happens.

kevin-runtime: I can pull traffic traces. On the routing side we have fallback policies that do region fallback -> variant fallback. If variant fallback returns a compatible model, we set cache namespace to model_alias only (bad) instead of model_id:variant_region.

jordan-sre: can you dump a few request traces showing cache keys and routing path? need examples to repro.

kevin-runtime: pasted 3 traces below (sanitized):
```
req-id: r-01
incoming: model=redwood-large@v1 region=eu-west-1
routing: primary->eu-west-1 (miss) -> fallback->global (hit variant v2)
cache_key_used: redwood-large
served_variant: v2
```
```
req-id: r-02
incoming: model=redwood-large@v1 region=eu-west-1
routing: primary->eu-west-1 (miss) -> fallback->global (hit variant v2)
cache_key_used: redwood-large
served_variant: v2
```
```
req-id: r-03
incoming: model=redwood-large@v1 region=eu-west-1
routing: primary->eu-west-1 (hit) -> served_variant: v1
cache_key_used: redwood-large_v1_eu-west-1
```

kevin-runtime: you can see the inconsistency: when fallback kicks in we drop the variant/region suffix and set a looser namespace so v2 responses get attributed to the base model key. That's the contamination.

tess-support: customer impact: Support reports 3 paying customers (AlphaFin, CartWave, EchoHealth) with high-confidence regressions in response style; alerting from SLO-monitor flagged elevated semantic-drift. CartWave already opened a critical ticket.

maria-ml: severity note — mismatch between served variant and pinned variant can cause hallucination/regression for customers who pinned to v1 for deterministic behavior. This is high-risk.

jordan-sre: immediate mitigation options I see: 1) disable variant fallthrough in routing policy for eu-west-1 to stop cross-variant reuse; 2) patch cache key construction to include full variant+region before any downstream caching layer; 3) purge contaminated cache namespaces. Which is fastest?

kevin-runtime: fastest is toggling policy to disable variant fallback for the affected service group. That avoids further contamination immediately and is reversible. Purge is possible but might be slow and heavy — better after we stop writes. Patch to key composition requires a canary deploy and tests, longer.

jordan-sre: ok do 1 now, 2 as follow-up, 3 after writes stop. Kevin, can you flip fallback off and confirm before I notify PS and customers?

kevin-runtime: running the toggle now. Using control-plane CLI: 
```
# disable variant fallthrough for service redwood-api-eu
rctl routing update --service redwood-api-eu --policy variant_fallback=false --reason "incident 1967890123"
```

kevin-runtime: response: 200 OK. Policy updated. Propagating to 3 control-plane nodes.

sam-engops: I see the control-plane changes hitting nodes. I'll watch for any cascading errors.

jordan-sre: verifying metrics...

(30s passes)

jordan-sre: metric check: 5xx rate in eu-west-1 dropped from 15% -> 3% over 2 mins. Misrouted served_variant counts show v2->v1 cross-answers trending to zero.

tess-support: notifying impacted customers: draft message posted to #support: 
"Hi — we're investigating responses coming from an unintended model variant due to a routing cache issue. We've applied a mitigation that should stop new regressions. We're rolling back queries and will follow up with an RCA. Apologies for disruption." :pray:

maria-ml: next step: we need to fix cache key generation in runtime and deploy to canary. I'll open a PR against runtime: include variant_id+region in cache namespace and add a unit test.

kevin-runtime: created branch: fix/cache-key-include-variant. Quick patch attached, exposes config flag cache.include_variant = true. Plan: canary to 10% of traffic in eu-west-1 after deploy.

jordan-sre: also request a targeted cache purge for contaminated keys to speed up recovery. Sam, can you run a sweep for keys matching pattern "redwood-large:*" that were written between 1967889600-1967890200 and remove only keys with missing variant suffix? Beware broad purges.

sam-engops: running safe purge script in dry-run mode first. Command: 
```
# list affected keys (dry-run)
redis-cli --scan --pattern "redwood-large*" | awk '{if($0 ~ /redwood-large$/) print $0}' > /tmp/candidates.txt
```

sam-engops: dry-run shows ~8k keys. I'll coordinate with kevin to pause writes before destructive purge.

kevin-runtime: to pause writes, we can put a temporary write-block at cache-writer layer: set env var CACHE_WRITES=false on redwood-cache-writer service. Deploy via k8s rollout to 3 pods.

kevin-runtime: running: 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/redwood-cache-writer CACHE_WRITES=false --record
kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-cache-writer -n infra
```

kevin-runtime: rollout success. writes paused.

sam-engops: performing purge now (targeted).

(30s passes)

sam-engops: purge complete. Removed ~7.9k keys. Post-purge check shows no recent writes for base-only keys.

kevin-runtime: re-enabling writes. 
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/redwood-cache-writer CACHE_WRITES=true --record
kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-cache-writer -n infra
```

kevin-runtime: writes back to normal.

maria-ml: canary deploy for cache-key patch continues. Observing 0 cross-variant reuse in canary. Tests pass. Scheduling full rollout after smoke window.

jordan-sre: summary for incident timeline: 
- 1967890123: Pager triggered by automatic monitors (misroute + 5xx spike).
- 1967890130: On-call acknowledged.
- 1967890145: Root cause suspected: cache key composition omitting variant/region when fallback path used.
- 1967890170: Mitigation: disabled variant fallback policy for redwood-api-eu (stop further contamination).
- 1967890230: Pause cache writes + targeted purge of contaminated keys (~7.9k).
- 1967890340: Re-enabled writes and canary-deployed patch to include variant in cache keys.

tess-support: customers notified. No escalations to execs yet.

maria-ml: action items: PR for key fix (KEVIN-124), postmortem with timeline and detection improvement (MARIA-341). Add a unit/regression test to alert if cache keys omit variant when fallback was used.

kevin-runtime: I'll follow up with a config flag to default include_variant=true for new services and update docs.

jordan-sre: handing off to Kevin/Maria for full recovery & postmortem. I'll remain available for any follow-up in this thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — mitigation complete and service stabilized. Incident severity: SEV2 -> follow-up required. Incident channel archived to read-only in 24h.

kevin-runtime: thanks everyone. logging notes and will file RCA tonight.

maria-ml: adding a quick eval: run a few prompt sets against pinned v1 to check semantic drift after recovery. scheduled for tomorrow morning.

(END OF THREAD)"
